title: Pattern captures never open a collapsed section, so half a sidebar is never photographed
foundBy: session agent, while updating the Explorer pattern for CUI-025
details:
`capturePatterns` clicks every expand-all control before it photographs a page, which expands the trees inside a section. It does not open a section that is collapsed, and SectionedTree keeps that state separately.

So the Explorer pattern's Dependencies section is never in a capture. Removing its filter box changed the rendered page and produced 0 differing pixels, confirmed by reverting the change and comparing both ways.

The fix is a few lines: click each section header whose control reports it collapsed, in the same place the expand-all clicks happen. It changes the baseline, so it wants its own pass rather than riding along with a content change.

notes.text: The same shape as the reason those captures expand trees at all: a pattern at rest hides the composition that is worth watching. This is the half of that argument the implementation missed.

The cause in `details` is wrong, and the fix it proposes is a no-op. Neither section on the Explorer page is collapsed: measured in the built preview, both `project` and `deps` render a `data-part="body"` at load. Teaching `capturePatterns` to click a collapsed section header was implemented and reverted, because it changed 0 of 94 captures.

What actually hides the section is the expand-all pass the capture already does. Measured at the capture's own 1440 by 798, after clicking expand all: the Project Files section grows to 1398px and pushes Dependencies to y=1695, inside a sidebar scroller that is 408px tall over 1615px of content. The section is scrolled out of view rather than collapsed, and a screenshot cannot reach it.

`assertNothingClipped` is right to stay quiet: the scroller does scroll, so a pointer can reach the content. This is a different gap, which is that the gate photographs one scroll position of a box that has several.

The fix is now a judgement rather than the few lines this record promised. A second capture with the sidebar scrolled to its end is the most faithful option and adds a frame per pattern. Expanding less would keep everything in view and give up the reason the captures expand at all. Photographing the scroller at its full height means rendering a layout the application never shows, which is the trap the comment above `assertNothingClipped` already warns about.
